title: Great God! the Heavens' Well Ordered Frame
description: Great God! the Heavens' Well Ordered Frame in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 168 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God revealed in his Works”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God! the heavens' well or-dered frame De-clares the glo-ry of thy name, There thy rich works of won-der shine: A thou-sand star-ry beau-ties there, A thou-sand ra-diant marks ap-pear, Of bound-less skill and power di-vine.

lines: Great God! the heavens' well ordered frame
Declares the glory of thy name,
There thy rich works of wonder shine:
Of boundless skill and power divine.
From night to day, from day to night,
The dawning and the dying light
Our thoughts to our Creator's praise,
And neither sound nor language need.
Far as the journeys of the sun:
Thy light and truth are known abroad;
We see thy smile in Nature's face,
And in the pages of thy grace
We read the glories of our God.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
